system: You are a security investigator reviewing an alert. Base every claim only on the evidence available to you. Cite the record IDs that support each observation.

supporting_observations.claim: At 13:28:03, a UserAssist registry value on WS-ICHEN-01 contains an ROT13-encoded path to powershell.exe under WindowsPowerShell v1.0.
At 13:39:46, WS-ICHEN-01 used the proxy to establish a successful tunnel to download.windowsupdate.com, with a Windows Update Agent user-agent and about 38.8 MB received.
The Windows Update traffic is consistent with the supplied context that workstation patching occurs during business hours, but does not establish that the PowerShell activity was part of patching.

At 13:38:15, the domain controller issued a Kerberos service ticket for sam.okafor to WS-ICHEN-01$, sourced from 10.40.10.23; this record does not establish a completed interactive logon or the purpose of the access.

The available endpoint records at 14:11 and 14:19 show short-lived SYSTEM conhost.exe processes, but do not identify PowerShell as their parent or establish that a visible PowerShell window appeared at the reported time.
At 13:31:56, FILE-NWD-01 connected to WS-ICHEN-01 on TCP port 135; the supplied record does not show what operation, if any, followed that connection.

known_telemetry_limitations: The supplied sensor-status information says WS-ICHEN-01 winsec and sysmon collection was unavailable from 13:30:00 through 14:10:00 UTC due to a collection outage. This covers the reported 13:40 window.
Proxy, Zeek connection, and Zeek DNS sensors are listed as operational, but those records do not provide the missing endpoint process details, PowerShell command line, or script contents.
The endpoint records before and after the outage cannot establish what process caused the reported window to appear during the gap.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually ran at approximately 13:40 UTC, and, if so, its command line, parent process, user context, and script or payload.
Whether the PowerShell activity was authorized patching or other benign administration, or unauthorized activity.
Whether the Kerberos ticket for sam.okafor corresponds to a successful remote session or is related to the reported window.
What operation followed the FILE-NWD-01 connection to WS-ICHEN-01 on TCP port 135.
Whether any files, credentials, or other data were accessed, changed, or transmitted as part of the activity.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover WS-ICHEN-01 endpoint telemetry for 13:30–14:10 UTC, especially process creation and termination, logon, PowerShell operational/script-block logs, and EDR process-tree data.
Check PowerShell history, transcripts, Prefetch, Amcache, and other execution artifacts on WS-ICHEN-01 for the relevant period.
Review WS-SOKAFOR-01 and FILE-NWD-01 endpoint and administrative records around 13:20–14:20 UTC to determine whether authorized remote patching or another administrative action occurred.
Obtain detailed RPC/SMB telemetry for the FILE-NWD-01 to WS-ICHEN-01 connection and determine whether any remote procedure or file operation followed.
Verify the purpose and outcome of the sam.okafor ticket to WS-ICHEN-01 against authentication and remote-session records.
Confirm with ivy.chen and IT whether a patching or support action was expected, and compare with change or deployment records.
